title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from pages 20–22. The setting is the profinite or discrete 'paradigm' of a punctured algebraic curve, as in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche. There is an extension 1 → π → Σ → 𝒢 → 1, with 𝒢 = Σ/π (arithmetically: geometric π_1, arithmetic π_1, Galois group). Σ acts on a set 𝒯, the cusps or 'points at infinity' of the universal cover. For each t ∈ 𝒯 there is a homomorphism φ(t): T → π, where T is commutative (think Ẑ(1)) and φ(t) maps T isomorphically onto the stabiliser π_t, the cuspidal inertia group. 𝒢 acts on T through a character χ (the cyclotomic character).

This page.
(1) Restricting the Σ-action on 𝒯 to π gives the action groupoid ⟨𝒯,π⟩. Its objects are the elements of 𝒯, and Isom(t,t') = π_{t→t'} = {λ ∈ π : λt = t'}. Its set of components is π_0 = 𝒯/π = J, the set of punctures, and the automorphism group at t is π_t.
(2) Suppose all π_t are commutative. Then for t' = λt, conjugation by λ gives an isomorphism π_t → π_{t'}. This does not depend on the choice of λ, because two choices differ by an element of the abelian group π_t. So one gets a 'transitive system of isomorphisms' among the π_t within each component.
(3) The isomorphisms φ_t: T ≅ π_t identify all of these groups with a single T. Grothendieck calls ⟨𝒯,π⟩ so equipped a 'T-groupoid': a groupoid, not necessarily connected, whose component fundamental groups are commutative and all identified with T. In modern terms, the components form an abelian-banded groupoid with band trivialised by T.
(4) Σ acts on this T-groupoid. It acts on objects by the given action on 𝒯, on arrows (elements of π) compatibly, i.e. by conjugation, and on T through 𝒢 via χ. The compatibility condition is σ·φ(t)(a)·σ⁻¹ = φ(σt)(χ(σ̄)a). Here π acts trivially on T, which is consistent with the conjugation-invariance in (2).
(5) Bracketed generalisation. Starting only from a Σ-action on 𝒯, one gets the groupoid ⟨𝒯,π⟩ with Σ acting on it. If this groupoid is abelian, its automorphism groups descend to a family of abelian groups (T_j)_{j∈J} indexed by J = 𝒯/π, i.e. a local system on the discrete set J. Σ acts on this family through Σ/π = 𝒢. One then supposes given a trivialisation T ≅ T_j compatible with the 𝒢-action via χ.

Purpose. This axiomatises, purely group- and groupoid-theoretically, the 'cuspidal/inertia structure plus orientation' of the fundamental group of an algebraic curve with punctures, together with its Galois action. Page 22 then maps ⟨𝒯,π⟩ to the groupoid of universal covers and records φ: 𝒯 → Hom_gr(T,π) as an (anti)equivariant map.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'transitive system of isomorphisms' is legitimate only because the π_t are assumed commutative. Grothendieck makes this assumption explicitly ('supposons T commutatif' on page 20, 'supposons ce groupoïde abélien' here).

One point is left implicit. For Σ to act on T 'via 𝒢', π must act trivially on the identified T. This holds because inner conjugation within a component induces the canonical identifications, but the page does not state it.

ideas.what: Action groupoid ⟨𝒯,π⟩ with π_0 = 𝒯/π and automorphism groups the stabilisers π_t
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Brandt, Ehresmann; Brown for the topological uses)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid), Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche (groupoids with base-point sets)

ideas.what: Abelian groupoid: automorphism groups canonically identified along a component, giving a local system of abelian groups (T_j) on J = π_0; a 'T-groupoid' is one whose band is trivialised by T
ideas.modern_name: abelian band (lien) of a groupoid/gerbe; T-banded groupoid
ideas.where_published: the notion of lien is in Giraud; the 'T-groupoïde' terminology is possibly in Pursuing Stacks / Longue Marche

ideas.what: Galois-type group Σ acting on the T-groupoid of cusps, with a character χ: 𝒢 → Aut(T) twisting the identification of inertia with T
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal inertia subgroups with Galois-equivariant (cyclotomic) orientation; Ẑ(1)-structure on cuspidal inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse/Longue Marche); developed by Nakamura, Ihara, Mochizuki (cuspidal inertia, combinatorial anabelian geometry)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discrete/profinite groups of type (g,ν) with inertia classes and orientation); La Longue Marche

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard formalisation of the cusp/inertia structure of a punctured curve's fundamental group with Galois action: an action groupoid, an abelian band trivialised by T, and a χ-twisted equivariance. These ingredients appear in Grothendieck's own Esquisse/Longue Marche setting and in later anabelian work. The 'T-groupoid' phrasing is a tidy repackaging, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The '11' at the top right is Grothendieck's own page number, not part of the text.
'[-$\equiv$-]' is a struck-through symbol before T. The reading is 'les identifier tous : on [...] T', i.e. identify them all with T.
'(i.e. un groupoïde (pas nécess. connexe) où les groupes fondamentaux des comp. connexes sont commutatifs et tous identifiés : T.)': the '[?]' after 'commutatifs' is probably spurious.

The opening of the bracketed paragraph likely reads 'Si Σ opère sur 𝒯, par restriction de l'op. à π [on] trouve un groupoïde ⟨𝒯,π⟩ sur lequel Σ opère'. This parallels 'Considérons la restriction de l'opération ... à π' on page 20. 'partiellement' is doubtful.
'Supposons ce groupoïde abélien, ... donc une famille' is probably 'Supposons ce groupoïde abélien, d'où donc une famille de groupes abéliens (T_j)_{j∈J} indexée par J = 𝒯/π'.
The line '(π-compos. ponctuelles)' is very uncertain. The sense is that Σ acts on the datum (𝒯,π): on 𝒯 by the given action, on π compatibly (by conjugation), and on T via 𝒢 via χ.
The last line is probably 'compatible avec les op[érations] de Σ (via 𝒢, χ)'. It continues on the next page with '𝒢 – lequel opère donc sur T'.
